subject: How to free AND give a starting value for a referent factor loading?

messages.author: 9044165ad6889125
messages.subject: How to free AND give a starting value for a referent factor loading?
parts:
What is the syntax that that I would need to write to both free and give a starting value for a referent factor loading? 

For instance, suppose I have a three indicator model with starting values.

 'c1 =~ start(.543)*x1 + start(.543)*x1 + start(.632)*x2 + start(.744)*x3'

Running this model generates the following error:

lavaan WARNING:
    the optimizer warns that a solution has NOT been found!

How might I tell lavaan that I want the first indicator to be freed? Note: applying std.lv = TRUE to the cfa() function does not work.

Thanks for your help!

Chris

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: How to free AND give a starting value for a referent factor loading?
parts:
You could explicitly free the first factor loading using NA:
 'c1 =~ NA*x1 + start(.543)*x1 + start(.632)*x2 + start(.744)*x3'

But you then must specify how to scale the factor. std.lv=T would accomplish that part.
You might achieve the same with the auto.fix.first=F" option.

parts:
Thanks Ed. Turns out that did help. I appear to have a new problem related to this issue now. 

I have three constructs in my model, each of which needs to have the same setup (referent indicator free, starting values added afterward). When I only apply your approach to the first construct, everything works fine. However, when I include the other two constructs, then I once again find that the optimizer does not find a solution. 

To reproduce my problem, here is my code:

ulmc.added <- ' 
  # define substantive factors with variable unstandardized loadings
c1 =~ NA*x1 + start(.543)*x1 + start(.632)*x2 + start(.744)*x3

c2 =~ NA*x4 + start(.543)*x4 + start(.632)*x5 + start(.744)*x6  
  c3 =~ NA*x7 + start(.543)*x7 + start(.632)*x8 + start(.744)*x9 

  # define a substantive relationship linking factor 1 to 2
  c2 ~~ start(.2)*c1
  c2 ~~ start(.3)*c3
  c1 ~~ start(.4)*c3
  
   # substantive factors standardized
  c1 ~~ 1*c1
  c2 ~~ 1*c2
  c3 ~~ 1*c3
  
  # ULMC
  ulmc =~ NA*x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
  ulmc ~~ 0*c1
  ulmc ~~ 0*c2
  ulmc ~~ 0*c3
  ulmc ~~ 1*ulmc
  
   # error variances for substantive factors
  x1 ~~ start(.632)*x1
  x2 ~~ start(.500)*x2
  x3 ~~ start(.308)*x3
  x4 ~~ start(.632)*x4
  x5 ~~ start(.500)*x5
  x6 ~~ start(.308)*x6
  x7 ~~ start(.632)*x7
  x8 ~~ start(.500)*x8
  x9 ~~ start(.308)*x9
'

# fit model for 100 people
fit1b <- cfa(ulmc.added, sample.cov = cov, sample.nobs = 500)

You should see that the optimizer does not find a solution. 

Note: If I remove the ULMC portion of the model, then everything runs. However, I need to figure out how to get the ULMC portion to run. I suspect that I will need to input starting values here as well?

Thanks for your help.

Chris

messages.subject: Re: How to free AND give a starting value for a referent factor loading?
parts:
Chris--
     I need to point out these lines:

# fit model for 100 people
fit1b <- cfa(ulmc.added, sample.cov = cov, sample.nobs = 500)

are inconsistent, 100 vs 500. But that is not your problem.

Estimating biofactor models is not easy. You don't provide starting values for the general factor loadings, but you may need to. In particular, if those loadings stay near 0, then the optimizer could be caught on the fringe of a mathematical black hole. You want to start those loadings at something like 0.2 standardized, and with the signs that you expect in the end.
